column1: # The sentences of clause 8.2 of TS 29.244 V19.6.0 that say which flags of an IE are set,
# as flag-sentences.tsv numbers them in their clauses: together, "at least one", "one and
# only one", "only one of", "may only be set", "shall be set to "1" if the ... flag is
# set", "shall not be set", "either ... shall be set", "exclusive" and "shall contain an
# IPv4 and/or IPv6 address", "an address"; with the field of
# another flag, "also present"; with the value of
# another field, "flags of a value"; with the Cause of the message, "with the Cause"; and
# always, "always set". A sentence of who
# sets a bit ("shall only be set by the CP function") is not of them. Each row gives the rule of check() that checks the sentence,
# in its words, with the octets of values of the IE of the clause that break it and that
# keep it, or `none:` and why check() cannot:
#   rule     the words of the Rule deviation of the clause that check() gives a value
#   breaks   values that break the sentence and nothing else: check() gives that
#            deviation alone; of a sentence "with the Cause", messages, checked on N4
#   keeps    values that keep it: check() gives no deviation
# The test `flag_rules` fails on a sentence without its row, a row of no sentence, and a
# value that check() does not answer as the row says.
